daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Rolling Volatility Analysis
daily_quests.description: Using ASX 200 historical price data, calculate the 20-day rolling standard deviation of daily returns for each stock ticker. Use a window function with PARTITION BY ticker and ORDER BY date to compute rolling volatility. Include ticker, date, closing price, daily return percentage, and the 20-day rolling volatility. Filter for stocks with at least 100 trading days of data. Order results by ticker and date. Expected output: a time-series view showing how volatility changes over time for each security.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning & Enrichment
daily_quests.description: Download NSW Road Crash Data (contains crash details, injuries, vehicle types, road conditions). Clean the dataset by: (1) removing rows with >30% missing values per record, (2) standardizing date/time formats, (3) converting categorical columns (crash type, road condition, severity) to consistent casing and removing leading/trailing spaces, (4) creating new features: day_of_week from crash date, hour_of_day from time, severity_category (group injury counts into 'minor', 'moderate', 'severe'), (5) detecting and handling outliers in latitude/longitude (keep only NSW bounds). Export cleaned data to CSV. Expected output: a clean, enriched CSV file with no duplicates, proper data types, and 3+ new derived columns.

daily_quests.title: Melbourne Pedestrian Traffic Peak Hour Detection Pipeline
daily_quests.description: End-to-end data engineering task: (1) Extract Melbourne pedestrian counting data from the Melbourne Open Data Portal (sensor IDs, hourly counts, locations). (2) Use Python/pandas to clean the data: handle missing values with forward-fill (max 2 consecutive), validate counts are non-negative, standardize location names. (3) Create a Python script to load cleaned data into a local SQLite database with tables: sensors (sensor_id, location, latitude, longitude) and hourly_counts (sensor_id, datetime, count). (4) Write SQL queries to: identify the top 5 peak hours (hour of day, 0-23) across all sensors by average pedestrian count, and rank sensors by their busiest hour. (5) Export results to CSV: one file for peak hours, one for sensor rankings. Expected output: SQLite database, 2 result CSVs, and documented Python script showing data pipeline logic.
